items.h: Not with starters in warmups
items.s: Tyson isn't working with the Saints' first-team offense pregame ahead of Sunday's contest against the Browns, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports. Tyson is active Sunday for the first time in his career, but the rookie first-round pick is getting reps before kickoff behind the WR trio of Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele and Bryce Lance. The Saints offense regularly has operated with three wide receivers this season, but it appears Tyson will be mixing in as a reserve rather than taking on a starter-level role in his NFL debut.

items.h: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) officially active for Week 9
items.s: Saints WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is officially active for a Week 9 matchup with the Browns. Tyson was listed as questionable after being a limited participant in practice this week. Tyson is set to make his debut Sunday, but fantasy managers should not expect to much as the Saints will likely slowly work him into the lineup.

items.h: Active for Sunday's game
items.s: Tyson (hamstring) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Browns, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports. Tyson, the eighth overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft, injured his hamstring in August, but now those who held onto to the highly-touted rookie during his absence a" or recently added him to their roster a" will going forward have a player with a high ceiling to consider for fantasy lineups. Given the long layoff, the Saints could choose to proceed deliberately with Tyson in his NFL regular-season debut, but as the season rolls along, the Arizona State product should yield dividends working alongside top pass-catcher Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele, who's been slotting in as the…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson Active for NFL Debut
items.s: New Orleans Saints rookie first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is officially active for his NFL debut on Sunday against the visiting Cleveland Browns in Week 9, according to Saints reporter Jeff Nowak. Despite being questionable all week in his return to practice, the Saints officially activated Tyson from IR on Saturday, and he will be a part of New Orleans' offense for the first time all year. The 22-year-old eighth overall pick from Arizona State injured his hamstring in August during training camp and missed the first eight weeks of the 2026 season. The big-play wideout is expected to eventually become the No. 2 WR in the Saints' offense across from Chris Olave, but…

items.h: Activated from injured reserve
items.s: Tyson (hamstring) was activated from injured reserve Saturday, but he remains questionable for Sunday's game against the Browns. Tyson thus is one step closer to making his NFL debut after missing the first eight weeks of the campaign due to hamstring issues that have bothered him since the start of training camp. With a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff on tap Sunday, his status will be clarified, one way or another, about 90 minutes before that point.

items.h: Inching closer to NFL debut
items.s: Tyson (hamstring) intends to make his NFL debut Sunday against the Browns, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz reports. The Saints opened Tyson's 21-day window in which to practice and potentially return from injured reserve Wednesday, and he managed three consecutive limited listings before getting a questionable tag for Week 9 action. The team still needs to officially activate Tyson from IR by 4:00 p.m. ET on Saturday in order for him to have a chance to play Sunday, but that appears as if it'll come to pass.

items.h: Jordyn Tyson Activated From Injured Reserve
items.s: New Orleans Saints wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) has been activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the Cleveland Browns. The eighth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft has yet to make his regular-season debut after suffering a hamstring injury during an August joint practice with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Tyson returned to practice Wednesday for the first time since the injury and was limited in all three sessions, including Friday's final practice. He remains officially questionable for Sunday. Tyson's arrival could eventually affect Devaughn Vele, who played 89% of New Orleans' offensive snaps in Week 7 and caught five passes for 54 yards and a…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson Should be "Good to Go" to Face Browns
items.s: New Orleans Saints rookie first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) plans to make his NFL debut on Sunday against the visiting Cleveland Browns in Week 9, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz. New Orleans listed Tyson as questionable on their final injury report for the week on Friday. Tyson, the eighth overall pick in this year's NFL Draft, has yet to play this year due to a lingering hamstring injury, but he "should be good to go" this weekend. The Saints will need to officially activate the 22-year-old pass-catcher from Injured Reserve on Saturday. Tyson was limited in all three practices this week after the Saints opened his 21-day practice window, which suggests he could…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson a Priority Addition in Redraft Leagues
items.s: New Orleans Saints wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) should be a priority waiver wire target for fantasy football managers ahead of Week 9 against the Cleveland Browns. While it's still unclear whether Tyson will actually be activated from injured reserve before Sunday's game, managers should get ahead of the waiver wire scrum and add Tyson now, if it's not too late. The 22-year-old rookie projects as New Orleans' No. 2 receiver and is already rostered in 58% of leagues, but there are still opportunities for managers to pick him up in shallower leagues. Tyson is a 2026 first-round pick, and he has the potential to immediately contribute as a WR3/flex option in his NFL debut, whether…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson Could Make Immediate Impact if Active Against Browns
items.s: New Orleans Saints rookie first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is listed as questionable to make his NFL debut in Week 9 against the Browns. He has put together a week of limited practices and will need to be officially activated from injured reserve to suit up. Once healthy, Tyson could slide into the WR2 role, with fellow receivers Devaughn Vele and Bryce Lance potentially seeing the biggest impact on their workloads. Tyson is a skilled route runner who can line up across the formation, totaling 1,812 receiving yards and 18 touchdowns over his final two seasons at Arizona State. He would be a welcome addition to a Saints offense that has looked stagnant at times. If…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) listed questionable Sunday
items.s: Jordyn Tyson is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Browns. Tyson was limited in his return to practice this week. He will have a chance to be activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday.

items.h: Listed questionable for Sunday
items.s: Tyson (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Browns, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports. With Tyson having logged limited practices after the Saints opened his 21-day window to return from injured reserve Wednesday, Friday's designation gives the rookie a chance to make his long-awaited regular-season NFL debut. There's been no indication one way or the other on what the Saints' plans are for Tyson this week. Devaughn Vele and Bryce Lance would be the biggest losers in terms of playing time and targets once Tyson does debut.

items.h: Jordyn Tyson Questionable for Week 9
items.s: New Orleans Saints rookie first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is considered questionable to come off Injured Reserve to make his NFL debut on Sunday against the Cleveland Browns, according to Saints reporter Jeff Nowak. Tyson was able to put in limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday, but it is unclear if he upgraded to a full practice on Friday, and it remains uncertain as to whether he will be cleared to make his NFL debut this weekend. While the eighth overall pick from Arizona State should be rostered in most fantasy football leagues now that he is on the verge of a return, we would caution that he will be an extremely volatile starting option in fantasy lineups if…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) limited in practice Thursday
items.s: Jordyn Tyson was officially limited in practice on Thursday. Tyson continues to trend towards having a chance to be activated for Sunday's game against the Browns.

items.h: Jordyn Tyson Limited in Practice Again on Thursday
items.s: New Orleans Saints rookie first-round tight end Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) was listed as a limited participant in practice on Thursday for the second straight day, according to Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football. However, Underhill added that Tyson does not look limited as he tries to convince the coaching staff that he is ready to come off Injured Reserve to make his NFL debut in Week 9 on Sunday against the visiting Cleveland Browns. The Saints are not going to rush the 22-year-old back, though, and they may require him to put in a full practice before they seriously consider activating the young pass-catcher from IR. If Tyson is active this weekend for his first NFL game, he will be an…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) practices Thursday
items.s: Jordyn Tyson practiced again on Thursday. Tyson was limited on Wednesday as he made his return to practice. It is unclear if he'll be activated by the Saints this week.

items.h: Remains limited Thursday
items.s: Tyson (hamstring) remained a limited participant at Thursday's practice, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports. Tyson has logged consecutive limited practices since having his 21-day window to return from IR opened Wednesday. The rookie first-round pick could make his NFL regular-season debut as soon as Sunday against the Browns, though the Saints may want him to log at least one full practice before seeing game action. For his part, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football suggested that from his point of view Tyson didn't look limited Thursday. In any case, the wideout's return to action, be it this week or next, would be proceeded by an official move adding him to the 53-man roster.

items.h: Jordyn Tyson Feels "More Explosive Than I Ever Have"
items.s: New Orleans Saints wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) told reporters that he feels "more explosive than I ever have" after returning from his hamstring injury. He said "I ran the fastest I ran since I been here in rehab...So I think I'm doing pretty good. I think I'm doing just fine." Tyson injured his hamstring in joint practices this preseason and was placed on IR. He was designated for return from injured reserve this week, and he could make his NFL debut as early as this week against the Browns, although the team has not officially addressed his status. The first-round pick has great fantasy upside in a pass-heavy offense, and is a great addition from the waiver wire or via trade…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) officially limited Wednesday
items.s: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) was officially limited at practice on Wednesday. The rookie was officially able to take part in New Orleans' practice on Wednesday. He has yet to make his NFL debut due to a nagging hamstring issue that he has been managing, but he seems to be close to full health and is officially in his 21-day practice window. Fantasy managers should keep close tabs on updates about his health, as he could be a relevant player down the stretch if he makes his NFL debut sooner rather than later.

items.h: Limited in return Wednesday
items.s: Tyson (hamstring) turned in a limited practice Wednesday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. This is a big step in the right direction for Tyson, whose 21-day practice window is now open. The rookie has been sidelined since late in camp with a significant hamstring injury. A limited practice after a long time away from the field does not guarantee he'll be ready to go for Sunday's game against the Browns. However, Tyson's debut is on the horizon, even if it is not this week.

items.h: Jordyn Tyson Limited in his Return to Practice on Wednesday
items.s: New Orleans Saints rookie first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) had his 21-day practice window to return from Injured Reserve opened on Wednesday, and he was listed as a limited participant in practice. Ongoing hamstring issues landed the 22-year-old on IR before the start of his rookie season in the NFL, but he has a chance to be officially activated later this week and make his debut in Week 9 at home against the visiting Cleveland Browns this Sunday. When fully healthy, Tyson was drafted to serve as the team's No. 2 pass-catcher across from Chris Olave. Tyson's return will be bad news for those who have Devaughn Vele rostered, but the rookie is not guaranteed to return this…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) will practice Wednesday
items.s: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) will practice on Wednesday, his first practice session with the team since injuring his hamstring in August. This is big news for the Saints offense and affected pass catchers. Devaughn Vele has been a viable option with Tyson out, but will see a target decrease as Tyson gets acclimated and playing time ramps up. Juwan Johnson could also see his target share suffer, but he has already been in a bit of decline. Still, Tyson should be usable for fantasy if not this week, certainly by the next.

items.h: Returning to practice Wednesday
items.s: Tyson (hamstring) is slated to resume practicing with the Saints on Wednesday, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports. The Saints are expected to officially open the wide receiver's 21-day evaluation window as they kick off Week 9 prep ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns. Given that the strained right hamstring has kept him off the field since Aug. 13, Tyson may need more than one week of practices to get himself back into playing shape, but the Saints haven't necessarily ruled the rookie first-round pick out from making his NFL debut against Cleveland. Whenever he's deemed ready to play, Tyson could immediately push Devaughn Vele for the Saints' No. 2 receiver job.

items.h: Jordyn Tyson Set to Return to Practice Wednesday
items.s: New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is set to return to practice Wednesday, according to Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football. The eighth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft has spent the entire regular season on injured reserve after suffering a hamstring injury during training camp in August. Tyson has yet to make his NFL debut, and his availability for Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the Cleveland Browns remains uncertain. Head coach Kellen Moore said Monday that the team was still evaluating when to resume Tyson's practice activities, making Wednesday's development an encouraging step in his recovery. Devaughn Vele has established himself alongside Chris…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) could practice Wednesday, status uncertain
items.s: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) could practice this week, but the Saints will determine his status on Wednesday. Tyson hasn't practiced or played yet since the season started, but it looks like he is clos to returning. They haven't fully committed to his return this week, but don't be surprised if he at least gets back on the practice field.

items.h: Uncertain to practice this week
items.s: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said that the Saints will decide by Wednesday whether to open Tyson's (hamstring) 21-day practice window this week, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports. Adam Schefter of ESPN reported over the weekend that Tyson could have a chance at making his NFL debut as soon as this coming Sunday against the Browns, but until the Saints formally clear the wideout to practice, a target date for him to play will remain somewhat muddled. The No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Tyson had a checkered medical history during his collegiate career, and the right hamstring strain he sustained in mid-August has only added to the long-term concerns about his…

items.h: Unclear if Jordyn Tyson Will Return to Practice This Week
items.s: New Orleans Saints head coach Kellen Moore said on Monday that it is still to be determined whether rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) will return to practice this week, according to Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football. The Saints will decide by Wednesday, which is when they will release their first official injury report for Week 9 as they come out of their bye. The 22-year-old eighth overall pick from Arizona State is eligible to come off Injured Reserve and play this Sunday against the Cleveland Browns, but it is unclear if that will happen yet as Tyson continues to recover from a lingering hamstring injury that has sidelined him for all of his rookie season so far in 2026.…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson Should be Rostered in All Leagues As He Nears Return
items.s: New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is nearing a return and should be rostered in all leagues. Tyson suffered a hamstring strain during a joint practice in August, prompting the team to place him on injured reserve. Although he has not played in the first seven weeks, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported a positive update, saying he could return as early as Week 9 and that he's not far from playing. The eighth overall pick in the 2026 draft totaled 136 receptions for 1817 yards and 19 touchdowns in his last 21 games with Arizona State. He would join wideouts Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele in the Saints' high-volume passing attack. While he could be limited upon his…

items.h: Could debut in Week 9
items.s: Tyson (hamstring) could be reinstated from injured reserve and make his season debut as soon as next Sunday versus the Browns, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. The Saints haven't cleared Tyson to practice since he strained his right hamstring during an Aug. 13 training camp workout, but the rookie first-round pick sounds like he could have his 21-day evaluation window opened in Week 9. Due to the length of his absence, Tyson may not be ready to play against Cleveland even if he checks out well in practice during the upcoming week, but in any case, he doesn't appear far away from making his NFL debut. Whenever he's activated, Tyson could push Devaughn Vele for the No. 2 receiver role behind…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson Could Make NFL Debut in Week 9
items.s: New Orleans Saints wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) could make his NFL debut in Week 9 against the Cleveland Browns, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. The rookie first-round pick has been sidelined since suffering a hamstring injury during an August joint practice with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Schefter reports that Tyson is nearing a return, even if he isn't ready for the November 8 matchup. The Saints have a Week 8 bye, giving the eighth overall pick additional recovery time. General manager Mickey Loomis said on October 21 that Tyson would not practice that week, making his potential return to the field an important development. Chris Olave has led New Orleans' receiving corps,…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson a Must-Stash Receiver Despite Delayed Recovery
items.s: New Orleans Saints wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) should continue to be stashed in all fantasy leagues, even though rostering him has required more patience than expected. Tyson opened the season on injured reserve, and it was initially reported that he would return around the end of September or the start of October. Instead, we're turning the calendar to November, and Tyson is still on IR. Stashing Tyson has definitely required more patience, but that patience should pay off when he does eventually make his NFL debut. The first-round pick is viewed as one of the most intriguing rookies in dynasty leagues, and he'll have similar upside in redraft fantasy football once he's…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson a Waiver-Wire Target Ahead of Potential Return
items.s: New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson is a player to watch on the waiver wire as he prepares to return. Tyson suffered a hamstring injury in August, expected to cost him two months. He was placed on injured reserve but traveled with the team to France for their Week 7 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. With the Saints heading into their Week 8 bye, many have speculated that Tyson could return to the lineup in Week 9, though the exact timing is unclear. The eighth overall pick is an unbelievable talent, totaling 1,817 yards and 19 touchdowns in 20 college games. With Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele operating as the top two receivers for quarterback Tyler Shough, Tyson may have…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson a Priority Stash Ahead of Anticipated Return
items.s: New Orleans Saints wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is likely nearing his activation from injured reserve, which makes him an appealing waiver wire target in fantasy football leagues. Tyson hasn't quite resumed practicing yet, but there's a strong chance that he gets back on the practice field next week in preparation for making his NFL debut midseason. The rookie's development was obviously hindered by the hamstring injury, so he may not be an immediate fantasy starter, but his first-round draft capital gives him tremendous upside, even in redraft leagues. Although Devaughn Vele has been playing well as the Saints' No. 2 receiver this year, there's a path to Tyson emerging as the…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) will not practice this week
items.s: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) will not return to practice this week. After being selected with the eighth-overall pick in this year's draft, Tyson has yet to make his NFL debut due to a hamstring injury. The rookie is progressing, but he is still not ready to get back on the practice field. Devaughn Vele and Chris Olave will continue to lead the Saints' WR corps.

items.h: Not slated to practice this week
items.s: Saints general manager Mickey Loomis said Tuesday that Tyson (hamstring) is "getting closer" but won't practice this week, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports. Tyson made the trip to Paris ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Steelers, but he's not ready to have his 21-day practice window opened just yet. While the Saints haven't provided many specifics regarding where Tyson stands in his recovery from a right hamstring strain beyond noting that he's "improving," the team has a bye coming Week 8, so rookie wideout will be afforded more time to get closer to 100 percent before potentially getting back on the field. If Tyson is able to resume practicing coming out of the bye week, he could…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson Will Not Practice This Week
items.s: New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) will not practice this week, according to general manager Mickey Loomis. Loomis said Tyson is improving and that the team is happy with his rehab progress, but he will not be activated. Tyson suffered a hamstring injury during a joint practice in August and was placed on injured reserve, with the expectation that he would miss multiple months. Although the rookie receiver made the trip to Paris ahead of their Week 7 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, he will be held out through the bye week, with hopes of suiting up in Week 9. Fantasy managers should continue to stash the 2026 eighth overall pick and expect Chris Olave,…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson a Must-Add Wherever Still Available
items.s: Already rostered in approximately two-thirds of redraft leagues, New Orleans Saints wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) may not be a name at the forefront of Week 7 waiver lists, but the rookie is a priority target wherever still available. While his return from Injured Reserve is not imminent, Tyson will reportedly travel with the team ahead of their Week 7 matchup with the Steelers to be played in Paris. With the Saints then scheduled for a Week 8 bye, the team may opt to take the cautious route with the eighth overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft, but Tyson boasts week-winning upside and could provide a jolt to a Saints offense that has struggled of late after a scorching-hot start to…

items.h: Makes trip to Paris for Week 7
items.s: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said that Tyson (hamstring) traveled to Paris in advance of Sunday's game against the Steelers, NewOrleans.football reports. Tyson has been sidelined since mid-August due to a right hamstring strain, but the Saints' decision to include him in their travel party to France could be a sign that his 21-day practice window will be opened this week. While Tyson would have a chance at making his NFL debut against the Steelers if he practices this week, the Saints may prefer to hold him out through their Week 8 bye to give him additional time to heal. Whenever he makes his way back from injured reserve, the No. 8 overall pick in the draft could immediately push…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson Traveling with Team to Paris in Week 7
items.s: New Orleans Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is traveling with the team to Paris for Week 7's international game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Tyson was placed on injured reserve with a hamstring injury expected to cost him about two months. While the team hasn't opened his practice window yet, Tyson appears to be nearing a return from the injury he suffered on August 13th. The rookie receiver was selected with the eighth overall pick in this year's draft and had 136 receptions for 1,812 yards and 19 touchdowns in 21 games with Arizona State. The Saints have a bye in Week 8, so there's a strong possibility the team is preparing for a Week 9 return. Fantasy managers…

items.h: Jordyn Tyson is a Great Stash Candidate
items.s: New Orleans Saints wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) will remain sidelined for the upcoming Week 6 matchup against the New York Giants. Tyson has been on the Injured Reserve all season after sustaining a hamstring strain in August. Saints head coach Kellen Moore said that Tyson isn't quite ready to practice yet. He did add that Tyson is progressing well, but he remains week-to-week. The Saints play the Steelers in Week 7 and then are on bye in Week 8. It seems possible that Tyson could make his season debut in Week 9, but that'll depend on how he progresses. Fantasy managers with an open IR spot should be stashing Tyson, with him likely returning sooner rather than later.

items.h: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) not ready to practice yet
items.s: Saints coach Kellen Moore said, "not right now" when asked if Jordyn Tyson could practice this week. Moore adds that Tyson is "progressing well." He remains week-to-week for now.
